mutations.rationale: Turn the sliding window into a fixed one: the whole bucket resets as soon as its oldest hit expires, so a caller gets `limit` at the end of one window and `limit` more immediately after -- 2x the configured rate across the boundary.
Measure the window with wall-clock time. A clock adjustment then either bypasses the limit (jump forward) or locks the caller out with no error naming why (jump back).
Make the read-only probe spend budget. A request refused for some OTHER reason then costs the host a slot, and the operator sees a rate-limit refusal whose cause was elsewhere entirely (B-02).
Evict an arbitrary (possibly ACTIVE) host to make room at the cap. Spraying distinct hostnames then resets every real host's counter: the memory bound becomes a rate-limit bypass.
Key on the un-canonicalised host. `split_url` leaves the root's trailing dot on, so `a.com.` and `a.com` become two buckets for one host -- silently doubling the rate for anyone who types it.
Admit limit+1 requests per window. Small enough to look like a rounding detail, and it makes the configured number wrong.
Give each port its own budget, so :80 and :443 each spend the full allowance against one origin -- the limit no longer protects the host it names (ADR-006).
Fail OPEN for a target with no host: an unkeyable target becomes unlimited, and the limiter disagrees with check_target's NO_HOST.
Report a whole window as the retry delay instead of the computed moment the window opens. A client that honours it sleeps far longer than required, which is how 'retry later' becomes useless.

method: The package is copied to a temp tree and the COPY is patched; the real module is never written. A survivor means the suite cannot detect that defect and the claim it protects is unproven.
